references.text: Describes how Jacob bought Esau's birthright, which is relevant for understanding why and how the deception in Genesis 27:35 could take place.
Jacob pretends to be Esau before his blind father Isaac and receives the blessing through deception—the very action Isaac describes in verse 35.
Jacob himself fears being exposed as a deceiver (מְתַעְתֵּעַ), which is directly linked to Isaac's statement that Jacob came with deceit (בְּמִרְמָה).
Esau reacts to the deception and points out that Jacob has taken both his birthright and his blessing—a direct follow-up to verse 35.
Hosea refers to how Jacob deceived his brother, connecting to the theme of Jacob's deceitful nature described here.
The consequences of Jacob's deception: Isaac sends Jacob away to find a wife among his relatives.
Thematic parallel: Both involve a brother losing his expected inheritance (blessing/kingdom) to another brother.
Clear thematic parallel: The brothers' jealousy and hostility toward the one who receives God's favor/blessing.
Typological parallel: Betrayal by someone close (a brother/disciple) who takes something that belongs to another.
